claim: CoT-style slow reasoning helps LLMs mainly on math, symbolic and logic tasks (mean gains +14.2, +12.3, +6.9 points) and is near zero elsewhere (56.8 vs 56.1); up to 95% of the MMLU gain is on questions with an equals sign. The fast/slow label adds nothing beyond task type.
schema_part: S1/S2 routing; operators gated by task type
agent_test: Run the same items at equal tokens with CoT forced on, forced off and routed; report gain by task class (calculation vs knowledge vs perception).

claim: Explicit reasoning can lower accuracy where verbal deliberation also hurts humans: implicit statistical learning (GPT-4o 87.5 to 64.4; o1-preview 57.7 vs GPT-4o 94.0 on a subset, a cross-model comparison), face recognition (64.0 to 51.2), exception-heavy classification (2.9 to 12.5 passes). Claude 3.5 Sonnet showed no significant drop, so the effect is model- and task-specific.
schema_part: G (no reflexive CoT); S1 direct-answer path
agent_test: Add a direct-answer arm on pattern and perception items; keep CoT only when it does not lose to direct on a held-out calibration set.

claim: Longer reasoning can lower accuracy and waste tokens: Claude Opus 4 fell from near 100% to about 85-90% as reasoning lengthened; DeepSeek R1 70% to 30% with five distractors; o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens on 2+3 and in over 92% of cases the first solution round was already correct.
schema_part: G (token cap); stop rule after first verified answer
agent_test: Cap reasoning at k tokens vs uncapped at equal total budget; test early stop after the first self-consistent answer.

claim: Reasoning models rarely need long thought on easy items: 28 reasoning models produced outputs 13.8 times longer than small LLMs; a 1.7B model without thinking exceeded 98% on easy sets; controlling thinking speed gave +1.3% accuracy at -8.6% tokens; 80.52% of GSM8K samples were solved more efficiently in normal mode.
agent_test: Test a difficulty probe that routes easy items to short mode; measure mis-routing cost on hard items (router transfer lost about 2.78 points).

claim: Distilling a rewrite-style System 2 method into a fast pass works (last-letter 30.0 to 98.0 at 25.5 vs 106.6 tokens; S2A bias task 51.6 to 81.3) but CoT on GSM8K could not be distilled (52.77 vs 7.13).
agent_test: Training is out of scope; test the analogue by caching verified rewrite templates in the scaffold and comparing at equal tokens.

claim: System 2 Attention (regenerate the context without distractor opinions or irrelevant sentences, then answer) removes distractor and sycophancy bias: 62.8 to 80.3 (oracle 82.0); GSM-IC 51.7 to 61.3. Single-pass prompt variants gain less (71.7). Gap search: a one-line instruction to ignore irrelevant information in a single pass matched distractor-example prompting on GSM-IC with code-davinci-002 (Shi et al. 2023), so the single-pass baseline must be beaten first; no equal-token test on a current frontier model was found.
agent_test: Add a clean-restate step; compare with a single-pass instruction at equal tokens on opinion-laden and irrelevant-sentence items.

claim: Plain debiasing prompts do not reliably fix LLM bias: an awareness prompt worsened the GPT-4 framing gap (-0.405 to -0.470) while counterfactual (-0.570) and self-help (-0.010) prompts changed it differently; GPT-4 gave correct reasoned answers on 69.2% of bias tasks vs 2.5% for Llama 2 7b.
agent_test: Compare debias prompts at equal tokens on a framing and anchoring battery with a no-prompt baseline and 10 draws per item.

claim: LLM scores on the CRT rose from trap-prone to near ceiling across generations (davinci-003 5% correct, 80% intuitive; ChatGPT-3.5 59%; GPT-4 96% vs humans 38-41%). CoT lifted davinci to 28%, but the newest model lost little without it (95 to 88%). The original CRT is a weak and likely contaminated test for frontier models.
agent_test: Use perturbed CRT variants (new items, altered numbers) rather than the original three.

claim: LLM answers on classic bias items are fragile to perturbation: GPT-3 answered 0.10 on all CRT items and kept 0.10 on an altered item; reordering Wason cards changed the answer; one changed number in maths cost about 18.3 points and algebraic letters left 20.9% accuracy.
agent_test: Ask each item under paraphrase and number perturbation; flag answers that flip and send them to a slower check.

claim: Human evidence for a speed-manipulation mechanism is weak: the time-pressure cooperation effect did not replicate (3,596 students, 21 labs, -0.37 points, CI -2.60 to 1.86; original +8.6), and the meta-analysis of load, time restriction and depletion on moral judgment gives g=0.06 (N=14,003), trim-and-fill g=-0.02.
agent_test: Do not assume speed manipulations transfer; judge design choices by accuracy at equal tokens, not by theory.

claim: The default-interventionist assumption (correct answers need slow deliberation) is challenged: about 90% of final correct answers were already correct at the first intuitive response in two-response studies, and about 74% of moral response pairs were utilitarian-utilitarian. Both figures rest on review text or memory.
agent_test: Log first vs final answer on a reasoning set; count how often the verify step turns a correct answer wrong.

claim: Conflict detection occurs even when the answer is biased: incorrect responders still lowered confidence about 10 points on conflict items (N=247 base-rate, N=147 conjunction), and conflict items are slow (medians above 30 s).
agent_test: Compare verbalised confidence on conflict vs no-conflict twin items; use the drop as a trigger for a slower check and test calibration.

claim: The CRT measures calculation more than reflection: in N=1,413 reflection added no unique power over calculation for framing or conjunction bias; it carries a sex gap (numerical d=0.39, N=66,109) and predicts job performance (rho=.36, N=1,508).
agent_test: Pair CRT-style agent items with numeracy-only controls to separate calculation from trap-resistance.

claim: Fast/slow agent designs give gains at lower cost on bespoke tasks: SwiftSage 84.7 vs ReAct 36.4 and Reflexion 45.3 on 30 ScienceWorld types at 757 vs 1,971-2,983 tokens per action; Dualformer slow mode 97.6% vs 93.3% with 45.5% fewer steps. These are system-level wins, not matched ablations of dual-process theory.
agent_test: Compare fast-only, slow-only and routed arms at equal tokens on our tasks; ablate the router.

claim: Interpolating between System 1 and System 2 alignment data changes accuracy monotonically; an entropy-based dynamic combination beat the base model on 11-12 of 13 benchmarks.
agent_test: Replicate with a prompt-only control at equal tokens.

claim: Moral dual-process evidence is item dependent: philosophers judged only 45-48% of items as real conflicts, dropping low-endorsement items removed the effect (McGuire 2009), deontological choice was 34% hypothetical vs 16% real (Bostyn 2018), and load had an effect at a 1:5 kill ratio but not 1:500.
agent_test: Treat moral dual-process claims as unsupported for design; one review source, primary papers not opened.

claim: Classic belief bias and matching-card findings (Evans 1983; Wason and Evans 1975) are recalled from memory only, with a response-bias reinterpretation by Dube et al. (2010). Gap search could not open the primary papers (paywall, rate limits); numbers remain unverified.
agent_test: Build a belief-conflict syllogism set; measure LLM acceptance of invalid believable conclusions with and without a belief-masking restate step.

claim: Same-model self-verification does not reliably fix first answers and often breaks them: GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after two self-correction rounds; Game of 24 5% to 3%, Graph Coloring 16% to 2% with an LLM verifier, but 38% and 38-44% with a sound verifier. A 2024 survey finds no prompted self-correction success outside tasks suited to it. Gains come from outside signals (tools, tests, labels).
schema_part: G (verification needs independent evidence); S-verify step
agent_test: Measure correct-to-wrong and wrong-to-correct flips of a verify pass on our model with and without a tool check; modern RL-trained reasoning models are untested in this evidence.

claim: Verbalised confidence is a poor trigger for slowing down: GPT-4 average AUROC 62.7% for failure prediction (GSM8K 54.8%), while 5-sample agreement reached 92.7% on GSM8K. After RLHF, verbalised confidence is better calibrated than logits on average (ECE cut by a relative 50%), but average calibration does not mean it separates right from wrong. The human conflict-detection confidence drop (De Neys) has not been tested on LLM conflict items.
agent_test: On a mixed item set, compare three triggers for going slow: stated confidence, sample disagreement, task-class rule; report AUROC for predicting that slow beats fast.

claim: Routing between short and long reasoning keeps accuracy at lower cost: ThinkSwitcher cut tokens 20-30% for 1-2 points of accuracy (14B 66.9 at 5,603 tokens vs BERT router 65.0 at 5,983); SynapseRoute 0.8390 vs thinking-always 0.8272 with 39.66% fewer tokens; about 58% of medical questions needed no thinking. No study holds total tokens equal across routed, always-fast and always-slow arms.
agent_test: Equal-total-token comparison of routed, always-fast, always-slow on a mixed set, with a mis-route cost report.

claim: A prompted token budget is not the analogue of human time pressure: models overshoot small budgets (50-token budget produced 157 tokens) and budget-aware prompting cut tokens 67% with under 3% accuracy loss. Only a hard generation cap tests the human time-pressure analogue; the human null (g=0.06) has not been compared with it.
agent_test: Run a hard max-token cap vs prompted budget on the same items and compare accuracy curves.

claim: Famous heuristics-and-biases items are contaminated for LLMs: GPT-3 gave the intuitive CRT answers but also answered a CRT with a nonsense premise with $0.10 and changed the Wason answer after reordering options. Evaluations of our agent need freshly written items.
agent_test: Build perturbed CRT and bias items (new surface, new numbers, nonsense premises) and compare to originals.
